newsitem.title: USA: U.S. zinc premiums still firm, lead creeps higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. zinc premiums still firm, lead creeps higher.

text.p: Although zinc and lead premiums remain firm in the United States, there are no signs yet of major tonnages wending their way from Europe to cash in on the healthy markets, traders said.

"Zinc is very tight in the U.S. at the moment," a New York trader said. "There is also a lot of activity in lead as the battery season starts - it's going to surprise a lot of people. I have been bearish for some months (in lead) but I have changed my mind."
Several zinc dealers noted that Sogem-Afrimet Inc, part of Belgum's Union Miniere, bought 4,061 tonnes of zinc in Wednesday's U.S. government stockpile sale of 5,726 tonnes.
There was speculation that one of Sogem's suppliers, Tennessee-based Savage Zinc, Inc part of Australia's Savage Resources, was experiencing production problems.

But David Rice, president and chief executive officer of Savage Zinc, said a "few hundred tonnes" of metal were lost due to roaster problems in August, but the plant is now back at full production of 105,000 tonnes a year.

Savage shipped over 10,000 tonnes to Sogem, its sole marketing agent, in September, and is looking to incrementally raise output by next year. "We are trying to squeeze a few more tonnes through," Rice said.
U.S. zinc premiums over LME cash remain at 5.50 to 6.50 cents per pound, with much of the business concluded around six cents, traders said.
Rice did not expect much change in overall zinc prices over the next six months.
Lead premiums over LME cash have edged up slightly to 3.50 to 4.00 cents per pound.

"Lead is tight and business is very good, but premiums are not high enough to attract foreign metal," said industry consultant David Cook of Lake Engineering. "All the producers are shipping right out of production."
The zinc market was awaiting the next U.S. Mint tender, expected within ten days to two weeks for about 4,000 to 4,500 tonnes.
One zinc dealer noted that strip jumbos in particular were in very good demand with supply tight. "Some people have already bought metal from Europe, but no great volume."
Some dealers said rumors that a large zinc position on LME, thought to be Spain's Asturiana de Zinc's position handed to Glencore International, has now been completely liquidated.
"This would be bullish for the market," a trader said.
